object_description: two separate volumes, a compact school building and a detached gymnasium
design_condition: the two volumes are set in the south-western corner of the plot, ringed by loosely scattered trees, with outdoor and sports areas terraced into the sloping topography by embankments and steps

positive: Loosely scattered trees convincingly mediate between the scale of the neighbourhood and the school buildings
Tree-lined peripheral areas offer sufficient space for recreation and play
Steps bridge the height differences and also serve as seating and recreation areas
Handling of space and topography is convincing through its pragmatic simplicity
The building duo forms a clear entrance and break area accessed from the street
Two-storey vestibule with flanking assembly hall and media library has an attractive outward and inward appearance
Three open staircases with adjoining atriums create exciting views and changes of light
The clear grid enables a good, clear and flexible layout of the rooms
The detached gymnasium avoids the complex statics of overbuilt halls and cleverly bridges a jump in the terrain
The free-standing hall allows natural lighting, ventilation and independent access for clubs or the neighbourhood
Textured rendering binds the two structures and refers to the inhomogeneous neighbourhood development
Simple and clear urban structuring, with a comprehensible extension shown for all stages
Compactness in section and plan with simple flexible construction promises cost-effective implementation
negative: The question of the identity and atmosphere of the site remains unanswered
Classrooms almost completely enclose the central zone, so only the building ends offer a view
Fragmented and restrained access zones will hardly meet the pedagogical requirements
The desired atmosphere in the building and in everyday school life remains difficult to read
The project cannot convincingly show the future face of the school or the next step in the pedagogical landscape
